Both of those functions use `K::Segment_3` to define the line segment between the two points and then call `tree.all_intersected_primitives` to find all intersected triangles. Since `numberIntersectedPrimitives` only needs the count, I can use a `std::vector` or `std::list` to collect the intersected primitive IDs and return the size of that collection.
